summary: Contains two corrections to RFC 2533, which defined a syntax for describing media feature sets: one fixes an error in the formal syntax and the other fixes a problem in the text. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo corrects two details in RFC 2533, which describes media feature sets. One fix clarifies the syntax for choosing a value or range; the other completes a rule for comparing features.

questions: what is a media feature set
what does slash mean in setentry syntax
subtitle: Two corrections to the media feature expression syntax and matching rules in RFC 2533.

tldr.problem: RFC 2533 contained an error in the formal syntax for set entries and an incomplete rule for reducing feature comparisons.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2738 corrects the setentry grammar and specifies the missing equal-value case in one matching rule.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2738 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2533; the syntax correction affects normative content.

today: RFC 2738 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 2533. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 2738.

sections.title: Two Corrections to RFC 2533
sections.content:
RFC 2533 defines expressions for describing media feature capabilities and an algorithm for finding common capabilities in two feature expressions. RFC 2738 corrects an error in the formal syntax and an incomplete rule in the feature-set matching reductions.

The RFC states that the syntax correction affects normative content, while the matching-rule correction affects non-normative content.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 2533 gives a way to describe and compare media capabilities. This memo fixes one syntax error and one incomplete comparison rule.

sections.title: The Set Entry Syntax
sections.content:
In the set-entry production from RFC 2533, the slash between value and range is a separator meaning either form is allowed. It is not a slash character that must appear in the expression. The corrected production is setentry = value / range.

This interpretation allows the set-expression examples in RFC 2533, including a list that combines individual values with a range.
sections.plainLanguage: A set entry can be a single value or a range. The slash in the grammar means “or”; it is not part of the text to write.

sections.title: The Feature Matching Rule
sections.content:
RFC 2533's rule for reducing the comparison (LE f a) (GE f b) was incomplete. RFC 2738 says the result is (LE f a) when a=b, and FALSE otherwise. This fills in the equal-value case.

The RFC notes that a revised feature-set matching algorithm was planned for testing and publication because the existing algorithm's results were not always in the most convenient form. Security considerations are discussed in RFC 2533 and related documents.
sections.plainLanguage: The old rule explained what to do when the compared values differed. This correction adds the result when they are equal.

references.text: Klyne, G., "A Syntax for Describing Media Feature Sets", RFC 2533, March 1999.
Crocker, D. and P. Overell, "Augmented BNF for Syntax Specifications: ABNF", RFC 2234, November 1997.
